rationale: Source investigation answers the reachability premise negatively for the fault model this code implements, so the Candidate is explained rather than escalated. handleCommit's NOOP-repropose branch dereferences inst.lb.clientProposals with no nil check (epaxos/epaxos.go:1092), and newInstanceDefault leaves lb nil, so the dereference would panic if it were reached with a placeholder. But the branch is guarded by commit.Replica == r.Id, i.e. the receiver is the row owner of the instance, and the row owner is the only creator of entries in its own row: handlePropose allocates into r.crtInstance[r.Id] (epaxos/epaxos.go:724-749) and startPhase1 installs InstanceSpace[replica][instance] together with a fresh LeaderBookkeeping (lb) before bcastPreAccept (epaxos/epaxos.go:751-779). Every other path that can produce a Commit for row R with a NOOP command goes through a recovery leader's startPhase1(preply.Replica, ...) (epaxos/epaxos.go:1307-1312), which only ever recovers an instance (R,i) that already existed, and an instance (R,i) can only originate from R's own proposal because handlePropose always uses r.Id. crtInstance[R] is likewise only advanced together with creating the entry. So in a crash-free execution the receiver's own-row entry always has non-nil lb, and the nil-lb placeholder state on one's own row requires the row owner to have lost its own instance, which is the durability/restart path (Durable false, replay unread) rather than a legal history of the modelled faults. The missing guard is a real latent robustness gap and I keep it visible as a remaining item, but I do not claim a reachable defect.

feedback.answered: The handleCommit nil-lb dereference is not reachable in the modelled fault model. The branch requires commit.Replica == r.Id, and the row owner is the sole creator of its own row's entries (handlePropose uses r.Id; startPhase1 installs the entry and its lb before broadcasting), while recovery (startPhase1 from handlePrepareReply sub-cases 5/6) only recovers instances that already existed. A NOOP Commit for one's own row therefore implies a row-owner entry with non-nil lb, so inst.lb.clientProposals cannot be dereferenced on a placeholder without the row owner having lost state (restart/durability).
remaining: Whether the durability/restart path can leave a row owner with a nil-lb placeholder for its own row, which would make the missing guard reachable; the replay path is unread (Durable is false by default).
handlePrepareReply evaluates lb := inst.lb before its inst == nil check (epaxos/epaxos.go:1206-1210); whether a PrepareReply can arrive for an unseen instance is a separate, unexamined premise.
A1 fast-path qualification and A2 ballot/authority transitions still have no executed check; quorum selection (A4) is unread.
feedback.rationale: Resolves the Candidate's premise with a sourced ownership argument instead of presuming a defect, and preserves the latent guard gap and the independent unknowns.

question.question: Can a Commit that carries a single NOOP for the receiver's own row reach handleCommit while the local instance is a placeholder with inst.lb == nil, so that the dereference inst.lb.clientProposals panics?
question.importance: Availability of a replica. Resolved as not reachable in the modelled fault model: the row owner is the only creator of its own row's entries and startPhase1 installs lb before the entry can be referenced by a Commit.
participants: row owner of the instance (commit.Replica == r.Id)
recovering coordinator that broadcast the NOOP commit
contexts: crash-free execution of the modelled protocol (no restart replay)
recovery restart with state.NOOP() when no Prepare reply carried a command
event_paths: handlePropose -> startPhase1 (entry and lb installed) -> PreAccept
handlePrepareReply sub-cases 5/6 -> startPhase1(state.NOOP()) -> commit -> bcastCommit with Replica = row owner
handleCommit: R receives its own-row NOOP commit; inst.lb is non-nil because R created the entry

supporting_behavior_ids.B-PHASE1: installs the row-owner entry together with its lb before any PreAccept is broadcast, which is why the own-row placeholder cannot arise without state loss
supporting_behavior_ids.B-PREPARE-REPLY-LEADER: generates the NOOP command on the recovery restart path but only for instances that already existed
supporting_behavior_ids.B-RECOVERY-START: creates placeholders for instances a replica has not yet materialised, but never for the row owner's own proposals

counterevidence: handleCommit returns early when inst.Status >= COMMITTED or commit.Ballot < inst.bal, but a placeholder has Status NONE and bal -1, so those guards do not protect this branch.

handlePrepareReply does check lb == nil (epaxos/epaxos.go:1210), so the placeholder state is expected elsewhere and the missing guard in handleCommit remains a latent robustness gap even though the modelled fault model does not reach it.
unknowns: Whether restart/durability replay can reconstruct a row owner's own row without lb, making the missing guard reachable.
question.trigger_rationale: The suspicion is a direct crash if reachable, so it was worth resolving the ownership premise rather than assuming either way; the sourced ownership argument shows the modelled execution never reaches it.
